A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoboPARA and X-DAPT. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained content to be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original X-DAPT evaluations, component ablations, and physical-robot experiments, including Tables 1–3 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds evaluations on six additional X-DAPT scenes, reorganized RoboTwin tasks, and execution-error recovery cases.

M1.justification: The two-stage planner, prompts, DAG validator, arm selector, and temporal scheduler remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–4. Appendix E.6 newly describes and tests rerunning the existing planner with updated observations after execution errors; it does not establish a revision to the planning algorithm.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates four X-DAPT scenes despite describing a ten-scene dataset. v2 adds supermarket, hospital, disaster rescue, hotel, pet shop, and library evaluations, plus regrouped RoboTwin tasks (Appendix E.5). It also evaluates interrupted execution through deliberately introduced kitchen-task failures.

E2.justification: Corresponding original experiments retain the same seven named baselines and their participation, including the Franka comparison renumbered from Table 10 to Table 19. Additional X-DAPT scenes reuse this set; the new RoboTwin comparison uses six existing baselines, without introducing a new comparison method.

E3.justification: The original 60-unit evaluation protocol is retained. New protocols regroup atomic RoboTwin tasks into scene-level combinations and difficulty categories (Table 12), and introduce specified execution errors into nine kitchen tasks (Appendix E.6). The worked recovery case imposes an apple-dropping failure at 12 seconds. These are additional evaluation designs, not established reruns of the original experiments.

E4.justification: The four original component ablations are unchanged. Appendix E.6 adds a distinct investigation of recovery from execution failures, with original and repaired schedules in Tables 16–17 and nine error cases in Table 18, covering dropped objects and a slipping knife across three difficulty levels.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Averaging over five cumulative task groups is retained. The nine new recovery cases are different tasks, not documented repeated trials or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 10–11 add six-scene results, Table 13 adds RoboTwin results, and Table 18 reports successful replanning in all nine error cases. RoboTwin TEI values for RoboPARA are 10.6, 5.2, and 2.4 across easy, medium, and hard tasks. Original Tables 1–3 and 8–9, and the retained Franka comparison, have unchanged numerical results.

T1.justification: The scheduling formulation, feasibility constraints, and metric formulas in Equations 1–12 are retained. The added architectural and global-planning discussions provide conceptual explanations, without new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a parallelism-focused scheduling problem, X-DAPT, and a two-stage RoboPARA planner improving efficiency and reliability. The headline execution-time and success-rate claims remain unchanged; additional experiments broaden their supporting evidence.

C2.justification: New Appendices C–D explain the division between symbolic planning and low-level physical feasibility, collision avoidance, and hardware-specific control, and discuss global versus reactive planning. Appendix E adds interpretations concerning cross-dataset generalization and recovery. The existing cost, accuracy, and skill-library limitations in Section 5.5 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2's abstract reports a public code repository where v1 promises release. Section 5.1 newly names ACT, DP, and pi0 as low-level action-model training algorithms, and the metric description explicitly includes planning time in TEI. A reproducibility statement consolidates resource information, while existing prompts, pseudocode, and retry limits are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds substantive System-1/System-2 positioning, locating RoboPARA within an established hierarchical architecture rather than retaining v1's broad final claim of a new planning class. Added references include dual-process foundations and hierarchical or constrained planning work by Holladay, Adu-Bredu, Vu, and Joublin. Other citations are added or removed beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the detailed methodology appendix remain closely matched. Changes include localized wording edits, author and affiliation updates, new acknowledgements and reproducibility/LLM-use statements, and appendix restructuring: new Appendices C–D precede the experimental appendix, formerly C and now E.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICLR layout and substantially redistributes displays. Figure 1 moves off the title page, and the GPT-4o heatmap moves from main-text Figure 4 to appendix Figure 7. Nine tables are added, covering new results and tabulated task/plan examples. Existing robot photographs, framework diagrams, and benchmark plots are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation that was limited in v1: it evaluates the remaining six X-DAPT scenes, adds an external dataset adapted for high-level planning, and investigates execution-error recovery. These additions address important gaps in coverage and robustness evidence while preserving the original results. Clearer planning-versus-control boundaries also improve interpretation. Recovery evidence remains qualitative and lacks repeated-run uncertainty, but the overall evidential improvement is substantial.
